title: Tenant-aware rolling upgrade orchestrator with health quorum
creator: Priya Shah
description: Goal: Build an automated, tenant-aware rolling upgrade orchestrator for Private (VPC) runtime/data plane upgrades that guarantees zero-downtime for healthy tenants and provides deterministic, fast rollback for impacted tenants. This ticket covers orchestration logic, Terraform/IaC hooks to coordinate control-plane config changes with data-plane node replacement, health quorum evaluation, and automated fallback policies. The orchestrator will be used for kernel/runtime binary upgrades, model-variant swaps, and config-driven runtime flags that require node restarts or pool replacements. It should interoperate with existing private operator and Terraform modules.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can perform tenant-scoped rolling upgrades without causing request errors above configured SLOs (default 99.5% per-tenant success during rollout)
Automated preflight smoke checks run per-tenant and gate traffic shift (connectivity, basic inference, prefix KV cache warmup)
Health quorum decision (N-of-M healthy replicas) implemented and configurable per-tenant/cluster size
Rollback triggers are actionable: latency/error thresholds, cluster-level resource pressure, and failed preflight checks cause partial or full rollback automatically
Terraform/IaC module hooks exposed so infra changes (instance type, disk mapping) are coordinated with orchestrator actions via plan/apply lifecycle
End-to-end tests (integration) demonstrate zero-downtime for a 50-tenant synthetic workload with mixed latency profiles
Documentation for runbook, operator API, and Terraform usage exists and is reviewed by PM and Security
Security review completed and secrets/KMS handling validated for private control-plane interactions
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Canary staging in internal env (1 tenant, 2 nodes) with full telemetry and tracing enabled. Phase 1: Tenant-sliced rolling upgrade in a single customer cluster using 10% traffic slice and primed KV cache handoff. Phase 2: Progressive expansion to 25%, 50%, then 100% of tenants in the cluster with health-quorum checks at each step. Traffic steering handled by Smart Router: shift only the tenant's slices to upgraded nodes once quorum reports healthy. Each step holds for a configurable observation window (default 5 minutes) and must meet health gates before continuing. Node replacement uses cordon/drain semantics with graceful shutdown hooks (kv-cache flush and pointer handoff). If any gate fails, orchestrator triggers rollback for the affected tenant slice and performs automated remediation investigation (collect logs, dump thread stacks) and creates an incident ticket linking to runtime logs.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback is triggered when: (a) per-tenant error rate increases >5x baseline for observation window, (b) p99 latency regresses beyond configured threshold, (c) disk or memory pressure exceeds safety margin, or (d) preflight smoke checks fail. Rollback steps: 1) mark upgraded nodes as drain-disabled for new traffic, 2) route affected tenant slices back to last-known-good nodes using routing policy, 3) if nodes are unhealthy, spawn replacement nodes from previous AMI/OCI image via Terraform with immediate join, 4) run post-rollback verification (smoke tests + load spike), 5) mark rollout as failed and create a retrospective artifact. Rollback is limited to tenant-scope unless telemetry indicates cluster-wide failure, in which case orchestrator escalates and halts all ongoing upgrades.
automation_notes: Terraform modules will expose lifecycle hooks: pre_apply (snapshot current runtime version + config), apply (update instance pool or tags), post_apply (signal orchestrator via webhook). Orchestrator implements an IaC-aware reconcile loop that verifies Terraform apply succeeded and then performs phased node replacement. We will implement plan-diff validations in CI to prevent instance type downgrades. A plan-lock mechanism will serialize concurrent upgrades to the same VPC. Operator endpoints: /orchestrate/upgrade (POST), /orchestrate/status (GET), /orchestrate/rollback (POST) with JWT auth via customer-managed KMS. For private installs, Terraform will inject a signed capability token into the control-plane to allow the orchestrator to act; tokens rotate per-release.
health_checks: Liveness: runtime main process alive + health API responds within 100ms
Readiness: can accept inference requests and return valid model outputs for a smoke prompt
KV cache priming: percent of prefixes in warm cache >= configured target
Resource checks: CPU, GPU memory, disk, and iowait under thresholds
Service-level traces: error rates, p50/p95/p99 latencies evaluated against per-tenant baselines
test_plan: Integration: synthetic tenants (50) with mixed traffic profiles, validate zero 5xx during phased rollout
Chaos: simulate node OOM mid-rollout and assert orchestrator isolates impacted tenant slices and rolls forward or back as configured
Performance: run soak test for 24h post-upgrade on primed cache scenario to ensure regression-free throughput
Security: pen-test the operator endpoints and ensure token rotation and KMS integrations prevent token replay
risks_mitigations: Risk: KV cache handoff may increase tail latency during handover. Mitigation: stagger handoffs and warm target nodes with prefix replay before traffic shift.
Risk: Terraform apply failures leave control-plane drift. Mitigation: implement plan-checker and revert-apply safety with immutable AMI fallbacks.
Risk: Tenant-specific resource hotspots cause partial outages. Mitigation: quota-aware upgrades and dynamic slot-reservation to guarantee minimum capacity for non-upgraded tenants.
Risk: Secret/token leakage between orchestrator and Terraform. Mitigation: ephemeral signed tokens + KMS-wrapped secrets and audit logs for every action.
definition_of_done: Automator can run a full rolling upgrade in staging and pass all acceptance criteria
Docs updated: runbook, Terraform module usage, operator API reference
End-to-end integration tests green in CI with synthetic tenant workload
Security review sign-off and secrets handling tested
On-call runbook created and paged escalation verified
